literal: Feigning anger, understanding, uniting - these (are) love united ones obtained fruit.
translation: Feigning anger, resolving it, and uniting in embrace: these are the fruits obtained by lovers who have come together.
modern: ஊடல் கொள்ளுதல், பின் அதனை உணர்ந்து தெளிதல், அதன்பின் கூடி மகிழ்தல் ஆகிய இவையே காதலில் ஒன்றுபட்டவர்கள் பெற்ற பயன்களாகும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the three stages of romantic bliss. First is 'ūṭal', the lovers' quarrel or feigned anger, which adds spice to the relationship. Next is 'uṇartal', the mutual understanding and resolution of the conflict. Finally comes 'puṇartal', the joyful reunion and physical embrace. The poet declares that experiencing these three phases is the true reward for lovers who have united in love.
